---
title: "7.11 Takeaway Points: Interactions and Cross-Model Comparisons"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

1. The identification assumptions of logit/probit (distribution of the errors) and the functional form restrictions (compression) cause the coefficients to be inappropriate as tests of interaction, mediation, and other cross-model comparisons
   - **Taking the methods you learned for linear models and applying them in the same way to nonlinear models can lead to incorrect conclusions**
   - Everything discussed in this section of the course is applicable to nonlinear linear regression models and all models for categorical DVs (e.g., binary logit/probit, ordinal logit/probit, multinomial logit, count models, etc.)
2. Predicted probabilities and average marginal effects are unaffected by the identification assumptions in logit/probit
   - MEs should generally be the focus of tests of interaction, mediation, and other cross-model comparisons
